text.p: Following are some of the main
stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified
these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Trades union federation FNV aims for four to five
percent wage rise in 1998 pay-and-conditions talks. (p1)
- Royal Dutch/Shell set to raise
profitability targets. (p1)
- Electronics firm Getronics sees higher
second-half profits. (p3)
- Securities broker Van der Hoop slams bourse plans
to raise capital adequacy requirements for brokers undertaking
their own clearing and settlement. (p7)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Government sets aside 160 million guilders for 'green' tax
breaks. (p1)
- Getronics seeks foreign acquisitions in case the
planned takeover of state-owned Roccade falls through. (p2)
- Loss-making PC maker Tulip says it could end the
year in the black after narrowing losses in the first half.
DE TELEGRAAF
- Cabinet seeks to curb tax deductions on pension annutiies.
- Transport minister Annemarie Jorritsma says touchdowns by
Dutch airlines should be exempted from Schiphol night flight
ban. (p7)
- Tobacco advertising expenditure in the Netherlands dropped
23.5 percentage points last year. (p21)
TROUW
- Supermarket chain Dirk van den Broek breaks the law by
selling below minimum price. (p7)
